seo.shortDescription: Searchable 2026 duty table for all 838 HTS Chapter 61 knitted apparel lines — T-shirts, sweaters, hoodies, leggings, underwear, socks, baby clothes, swimwear, gloves — with General, FTA and Column 2 rates and the extra duty for Vietnam, China, Cambodia, Bangladesh, India and CAFTA-DR suppliers.

overview.intro:
Chapter 61 covers clothing and accessories that are **knitted or crocheted**: coats and anoraks (6101–6102), suits, ensembles, trousers, leggings, dresses and skirts (6103–6104), knit shirts and blouses (6105–6106), underwear and sleepwear (6107–6108), **T-shirts** (6109), **sweaters, sweatshirts and hoodies** (6110), babies' clothing (6111), track suits and swimwear (6112), other garments (6113–6114), **socks and hosiery** (6115), gloves (6116) and scarves and other accessories (6117). Woven garments are Chapter 62. Its **838 lines** carry some of the highest base rates in the schedule, and the rate turns on **fibre and garment type**: a cotton T-shirt or sweatshirt is 16.5%, the same T-shirt or sweater of man-made fibres **32%**, cotton socks 13.5%, a cashmere sweater 4%. Knit suit ensembles (6103.2x, 6104.2x) have no rate of their own: each garment pays the rate it would pay if entered separately.

On top of the base rate, since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** — Vietnam, Egypt and the Dominican Republic 12.5%, Cambodia, Bangladesh, Indonesia, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka 10%. **China pays 12.5% plus 7.5%** under List 4A on 714 of the 838 lines. Apparel entered duty-free under **CAFTA-DR** (Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic, Costa Rica) and **Jordan's** apparel are exempt, and USMCA goods pay nothing extra — except six Canadian subheadings, including cotton T-shirts and sweaters, that owe **50% under Section 338** even with USMCA. The U.S. imported **$46.64B** of knitted apparel in 2025: Vietnam $9.84B, China $6.81B, Cambodia $3.67B, Bangladesh $2.97B.

productGroups.label: Men's and boys' knit coats, anoraks, ski jackets and windbreakers
productGroups.blurb: Men's and boys' knit overcoats, anoraks, ski jackets, windbreakers and similar outerwear (not suit jackets): cotton 15.9%, man-made fibres 28.2%, wool 61.7¢/kg + 16%. Fleece jackets of polyester are 6101.30.20.

productGroups.label: Women's and girls' knit coats, anoraks, ski jackets and windbreakers
productGroups.blurb: The same outerwear for women and girls: cotton 15.9%, man-made fibres 28.2%, wool 55.9¢/kg + 16.4%. Garments that close right over left are women's (chapter note 9).

productGroups.label: Men's and boys' knit suits, ensembles, blazers, trousers and shorts
productGroups.blurb: Men's and boys' knit suits, ensembles, suit-type jackets and blazers, trousers and shorts. Cotton trousers and shorts 16.1%, synthetic 28.2%; cotton blazers 13.5%. Ensembles (6103.22–6103.29) pay each garment's own rate.

productGroups.label: Women's and girls' knit suits, ensembles, dresses, skirts, trousers, leggings and shorts
productGroups.blurb: Women's and girls' knit suits, ensembles, jackets, dresses, skirts, trousers, leggings and shorts. Synthetic trousers and leggings 28.2%, cotton 14.9%; cotton dresses 11.5%, synthetic 16%; cotton skirts 8.3%. Ensembles (6104.22–6104.29) pay each garment's own rate.

productGroups.label: Men's and boys' knit shirts (polo shirts)
productGroups.blurb: Men's and boys' knit shirts with a neckline opening, such as polo shirts: cotton 19.7%, man-made fibres 32%. Garments with a ribbed waistband or under 10 stitches per cm are not here (chapter note 4).

productGroups.label: Women's and girls' knit blouses and shirts
productGroups.blurb: Women's and girls' knit blouses and shirts: cotton 19.7%, man-made fibres 32%, wool 13.6%, silk 0.9%.

productGroups.label: Men's and boys' underwear, pajamas and bathrobes, knit
productGroups.blurb: Men's and boys' underpants, briefs, boxers, nightshirts, pajamas, bathrobes and dressing gowns: cotton briefs 7.4%, man-made fibre briefs 14.9%, cotton pajamas 8.9%, man-made fibre pajamas 16%.

productGroups.label: Women's and girls' slips, panties, nightdresses, pajamas and robes, knit
productGroups.blurb: Women's and girls' slips, briefs and panties, nightdresses, pajamas, negligees and robes: cotton panties 7.6%, man-made fibre panties 15.6%, cotton nightwear 8.5%, man-made fibre nightwear 16%. Bras are heading 6212.

productGroups.label: T-shirts, singlets and tank tops, knit
productGroups.blurb: T-shirts, singlets and tank tops — the largest-volume knit line. Cotton 16.5%, man-made fibres 32%. Garments with a drawstring or ribbed waistband at the bottom are not T-shirts (chapter note 5).

productGroups.label: Sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, hoodies, cardigans and vests, knit
productGroups.blurb: Sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, hoodies, cardigans and vests — the chapter's largest heading by value. Cotton 16.5%, man-made fibres 32%, wool 16%, wholly cashmere 4%. Sweatshirts and hoodies are statistical lines of 6110.20.20 (cotton) and 6110.30.30 (man-made fibres).

productGroups.label: Babies' garments and clothing accessories, knit
productGroups.blurb: Garments and accessories for babies — body height up to 86 cm (chapter note 6), which take this heading before any other: cotton sets, sunsuits and other babies' wear 8.1%, cotton T-shirts and trousers 14.9%, synthetic T-shirts and shirts 32%.

productGroups.label: Track suits, ski suits and swimwear, knit
productGroups.blurb: Track suits, ski suits and swimwear. Cotton track suits 14.9%, synthetic 28.2%; men's synthetic swimwear 25.9%, women's synthetic swimwear and bikinis 24.9%.

productGroups.label: Garments of coated, rubberized or laminated knit fabric
productGroups.blurb: Garments of knit fabric that is coated, covered or laminated with rubber or plastics (heading 5903, 5906 or 5907): 3.8% or 7.1%. This heading wins over the other headings of the chapter except babies' wear (note 8).

productGroups.label: Other knit garments (tops, bodysuits, jumpsuits, scrubs)
productGroups.blurb: Knit garments not covered elsewhere — tops, bodysuits, jumpsuits, scrubs and coveralls. Cotton 10.8%; man-made fibre tops 28.2%, bodysuits 32%, other 14.9%.

productGroups.label: Socks, tights, pantyhose and other hosiery, knit
productGroups.blurb: Socks, tights, pantyhose, stockings and compression hosiery, including footwear without applied soles. Cotton socks 13.5%, synthetic socks 14.6% (18.8% with lace), pantyhose 16%; surgical compression stockings Free.

productGroups.label: Gloves, mittens and mitts, knit
productGroups.blurb: Knit gloves, mittens and mitts: synthetic gloves 18.6%, cotton machine-knit 23.5% or 9.4%, coated work gloves 7%–23.5%, ice- and field-hockey gloves Free. Leather gloves are 4203, rubber and nitrile gloves 4015.

productGroups.label: Scarves, shawls, ties, headbands and other knit accessories; parts
productGroups.blurb: Scarves, shawls, mufflers and veils, ties, headbands and other made-up knit accessories, and knit parts of garments: man-made fibre scarves 11.3%, headbands and other accessories 14.6%, ties 5%.

rateTable.note: Rates shown in grey are inherited from the parent heading. HTSUS states a duty once on the 8-digit line and leaves the 10-digit statistical lines blank; this table resolves each line to the rate that actually applies to it.

workedExamples.title: Cotton T-shirts from Vietnam
workedExamples.body: Men's cotton T-shirts are 16.5% at the general rate, and Vietnam adds 12.5% Section 301 (9903.05.84): **29%**, $2,900 on a $10,000 shipment. The same T-shirts pay 26.5% from Bangladesh, Cambodia or India, 36.5% from China (List 4A adds 7.5%), and nothing from Honduras or Guatemala under CAFTA-DR. In late 2025 Vietnam's rate was 36.5% (20% IEEPA).

workedExamples.title: Polyester sweatshirts and hoodies from China
workedExamples.body: Man-made-fibre sweatshirts carry the chapter's top rate, 32%. China adds 12.5% (9903.05.31) and 7.5% under List 4A (9903.88.15): **52%**, $5,200 on $10,000. From Cambodia the same hoodies pay 42%; a cotton hoodie (6110.20.20.41, 16.5%) from China pays 36.5%. The fibre that predominates by weight decides the line.

workedExamples.title: Men's cotton knit ensemble from China — priced garment by garment
workedExamples.body: 6103.22.00's rate is "the rate applicable to each garment in the ensemble if separately entered". For a $10,000 shipment of jackets ($6,000, 6103.32.00, 13.5%) and matching trousers ($4,000, 6103.42.10, 16.1%) the base duty is $810 + $644 = $1,454. China's 12.5% and 7.5% apply to the whole $10,000 ($2,000): **$3,454**. The calculator asks for each garment's 10-digit line and value; the values must add up to the shipment value.

workedExamples.title: Cotton T-shirts from Honduras under CAFTA-DR
workedExamples.body: With a CAFTA-DR claim (SPI P) the base rate is Free, and CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods entered free of duty are exempt from the 10% Section 301 duty (note 52(i), 9903.05.95): **$0**. Without the claim — for example T-shirts sewn from Asian fabric that do not meet the yarn-forward rule — they pay 16.5% + 10% = 26.5% ($2,650).

workedExamples.title: Cotton sweatshirts from Canada, with a USMCA claim
workedExamples.body: USMCA removes the 16.5% base rate and the 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93). But 6110.20.20 is on the Section 338 list (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14), whose 50% applies even with USMCA: **$5,000** on $10,000. Without a USMCA claim: 16.5% + 10% + 50% = 76.5%. Mexican USMCA sweatshirts pay nothing.

workedExamples.title: Cotton socks from Pakistan
workedExamples.body: Cotton socks without lace are 13.5%, plus 10% Section 301 for Pakistan (9903.05.62): **23.5%**, $2,350 on $10,000. From China they pay 33.5%; from Jordan they are Free (JO, and Jordan's exception list); from Italy 13.5% (the EU's 10% in-total rate is below the base rate).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** This chapter applies only to made up knitted or crocheted articles.

**Note 2.** It does not cover goods of heading 6212 (bras, girdles, corsets, suspenders), worn clothing of heading 6309, or orthopedic appliances, surgical belts and trusses (heading 9021).

**Note 3.** For headings 6103 and 6104: (a) a **suit** is a set of two or three pieces with an outer surface of identical fabric — a suit coat or jacket of four or more panels (with or without a tailored waistcoat) and trousers, breeches, shorts (not swimwear), a skirt or a divided skirt — of the same fabric construction, color, composition and style; morning dress, evening dress and dinner-jacket suits are suits too. (b) An **ensemble** is a set of garments of identical fabric, put up for retail sale, of one upper garment (a pullover may be a second upper garment only in a twin set, and a waistcoat may also be a second one) and one or two different lower garments (trousers, bib and brace overalls, breeches, shorts, a skirt or a divided skirt), all of the same fabric construction, style, color and composition and of corresponding size. Articles of 6107, 6108 and 6109, track suits and ski suits are not ensembles.

**Note 4.** Headings 6105 and 6106 do not cover garments with pockets below the waist, a ribbed waistband or other tightening at the bottom, or under 10 stitches per linear cm in each direction; 6105 does not cover sleeveless garments.

**Note 5.** Heading 6109 does not cover garments with a drawstring, ribbed waistband or other tightening at the bottom.

**Note 6.** "Babies' garments" (6111) are for young children of a body height not over 86 cm, and articles classifiable both in 6111 and elsewhere in the chapter go to 6111.

**Note 7.** "Ski-suits" (6112) are ski overalls, or ski ensembles of an anorak or windbreaker closed by a zipper and trousers, breeches or a bib and brace overall.

**Note 8.** Garments classifiable both in 6113 (coated or laminated fabric) and elsewhere, except 6111, go to 6113.

**Note 9.** Garments closing left over right are men's or boys', right over left women's or girls', unless the cut clearly shows otherwise; garments that cannot be identified as either are classified as women's or girls'.

**Note 10.** Articles of this chapter may be made of metal thread.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**Additional U.S. note 1.** For heading 6111, "sets" means two or more different garments of headings 6111, 6209 or 6505 imported together, of corresponding sizes and intended to be worn together by the same person.

**Statistical notes.** (1) Garments entered together and classified as an ensemble (6103.21–6103.29.10, 6104.21–6104.29.10) or a track suit (6112.11, 6112.12) are reported as separate articles under the most appropriate 10-digit number within the same 8-digit subheading. (2) For 6103, 6104 and 6112, "shirts" means garments of 6105, 6106 and 6110 other than sweaters. (3) "Sweaters" are garments whose outer surface has 9 or fewer stitches per 2 cm in the direction the stitches were formed. (4) Garments assembled abroad from U.S.-formed and cut components and then bleached, garment-dyed or perma-pressed may enter under a Special Access Regime, reported with the prefix "H". (5) Garments cut and assembled from U.S.-formed fabric under the Outward Processing Program are reported with the prefix "S". (6) "Knit to shape" in 6110 means garments knit to shape on flat-knitting machines with 10 to 18 stitches per 2 cm, all components knit to shape and assembled by looping and linking.

The three-digit numbers in brackets (for example 338 cotton knit shirts, 345 cotton sweaters, 645 man-made-fibre sweaters) are textile category numbers used to monitor shipments and to count AGOA, Haiti and USMCA quantity limits. No Chapter 61 line carries a footnote to the Russia heading 9903.90.08.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for U.S. knitted apparel tariffs since January 2025: the end of the IEEPA duties and the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies (Vietnam +12.5%, Cambodia and Bangladesh +10%), the CAFTA-DR and Jordan exemptions, China List 4A, Canada's Section 338 duty on T-shirts and sweaters, AGOA and Haiti renewals and the end of de minimis.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 61 base rate changed**: all 838 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates, from Free to 32% and compound rates such as 61.7¢/kg + 16%.

Everything that changed sits on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA duties reached every garment — 20% for Vietnam, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, 19% for Cambodia, Indonesia and Pakistan, 50% for India from August 27, 2025, and up to 125% plus 20% for China in April–May 2025. They **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff** of 10% or 12.5%, but **CAFTA-DR apparel entered duty-free is exempt** (note 52(i)) and **Jordan's** exception list covers almost every Chapter 61 subheading. China still pays **+7.5% (List 4A)** on 714 lines, and since **August 22, 2026** six Canadian subheadings — cotton T-shirts, cotton and man-made-fibre sweaters, women's synthetic dresses and trousers, synthetic gloves — owe a **50% Section 338 duty** even under USMCA. AGOA and the Haiti HOPE/HELP programs were renewed through December 31, 2026, and the $800 de minimis exemption stays suspended, so apparel shipped direct to consumers pays full duty.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 61 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their CAFTA-DR, Jordan, Guatemala and El Salvador exemptions; the Brazil Section 301 tariff; China Section 301 List 4A, its babies'-sleep-sack exclusion and the suspended List 4B; the Canada Section 338 duty; the Nicaragua Section 301 duty scheduled for 2027; the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended; and the suspension of de minimis. Preference-program changes (AGOA, Haiti HOPE/HELP, GSP, USMCA review) and the UFLPA forced-labor rules are listed for reference. No Section 232 action and no antidumping or countervailing duty order covers a Chapter 61 product. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 61 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or on a country exception list for Vietnam. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. Vietnam's IEEPA rate had been 20% (9903.02.69) from August 7, 2025.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese cotton T-shirts and sweatshirts pay 29% (16.5% + 12.5%), polyester sweaters and hoodies 44.5%, synthetic leggings 40.7%.

inEffect.now: +20% on 714 lines; +12.5% on the 124 former List 4B lines
inEffect.exemption: Two Section 301 duties stack: +12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31) on every line, and +7.5% under List 4A (9903.88.15, U.S. note 20(s)) on 209 subheadings, 714 of the 838 lines. The other 43 of the chapter's 252 eight-digit subheadings (124 of the 838 lines) — mostly silk, cashmere, wool-blend and artificial-fibre lines, hockey and other special gloves, surgical compression hosiery and ties — were put on List 4B (9903.88.16), which never took effect, so they pay only 12.5%. One List 4A exclusion (9903.88.69, note 20(vvv)(iv)) runs through November 9, 2026: babies' knit cotton sleep sacks with a neck opening and two-way zipper (6111.20.60.70). USTR's four-year review kept List 4A in place. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.

inEffect.exemption: CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods (general note 29(d)(v)) of Honduras entered free of duty under CAFTA-DR — SPI P, or a subchapter XXII Chapter 98 provision such as short-supply heading 9822.05.01 — pay no Section 301 duty (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). That covers 821 of the 838 lines. The other 17 lines whose General rate is already Free — suits of artificial fibres and wool-blend synthetic suits (6103.10.40, .50, 6104.13.10, 6104.19.15), women's suit-type jackets of other textiles (6104.39.20), artificial-fibre babies' T-shirts (6111.90.30), surgical compression hosiery (6115.10.05), and ice- and field-hockey gloves and silk gloves (6116.10.05, .92.05, .93.05, .99.20, .99.75) — print no P rate, so they cannot be entered under CAFTA-DR and pay the duty. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. Honduras's IEEPA rate had been the 10% baseline.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Honduran T-shirts, sweatshirts and socks that qualify under CAFTA-DR enter with no duty at all; non-qualifying goods pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 tariff (2026, 60 economies); CAFTA-DR apparel exempt
inEffect.exemption: CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods (general note 29(d)(v)) of Nicaragua entered free of duty under CAFTA-DR — SPI P, or a subchapter XXII Chapter 98 provision such as short-supply heading 9822.05.01 — pay no Section 301 duty (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). That covers 821 of the 838 lines. The other 17 lines whose General rate is already Free — suits of artificial fibres and wool-blend synthetic suits (6103.10.40, .50, 6104.13.10, 6104.19.15), women's suit-type jackets of other textiles (6104.39.20), artificial-fibre babies' T-shirts (6111.90.30), surgical compression hosiery (6115.10.05), and ice- and field-hockey gloves and silk gloves (6116.10.05, .92.05, .93.05, .99.20, .99.75) — print no P rate, so they cannot be entered under CAFTA-DR and pay the duty. Separately, Nicaraguan goods not entered under CAFTA-DR will pay a Nicaragua Section 301 duty (9903.89.01) of 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. Nicaragua's IEEPA rate had been 18% (9903.02.47); The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: CAFTA-DR-qualifying Nicaraguan apparel pays nothing; non-qualifying goods pay the base rate plus 12.5% now, and 10% more from 2027.

inEffect.exemption: Jordan's exception list (note 52(j), 9903.06.20) and, when CAFTA-DR is claimed, the Guatemala and El Salvador lists (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09) cover 245 of the 252 Chapter 61 subheadings — every one except graduated compression hosiery (6115.10). For Jordan the list applies whether or not the US–Jordan FTA is claimed, so only graduated compression hosiery (6115.10, 9 lines) pays the 10% (9903.05.50). Jordan's IEEPA rate had been 15% (9903.02.31); The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Jordanian apparel under the US–Jordan FTA (SPI JO) enters Free with no extra duty; compression socks pay 10%.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 61 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or on a country exception list for Pakistan. GSP has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. Pakistan's IEEPA rate had been 19%.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Pakistani cotton socks pay 23.5%, cotton T-shirts 26.5%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 tariff (2026, 60 economies); CAFTA-DR apparel exempt
inEffect.exemption: CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods (general note 29(d)(v)) of Guatemala entered free of duty under CAFTA-DR — SPI P, or a subchapter XXII Chapter 98 provision such as short-supply heading 9822.05.01 — pay no Section 301 duty (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). That covers 821 of the 838 lines. The other 17 lines whose General rate is already Free — suits of artificial fibres and wool-blend synthetic suits (6103.10.40, .50, 6104.13.10, 6104.19.15), women's suit-type jackets of other textiles (6104.39.20), artificial-fibre babies' T-shirts (6111.90.30), surgical compression hosiery (6115.10.05), and ice- and field-hockey gloves and silk gloves (6116.10.05, .92.05, .93.05, .99.20, .99.75) — print no P rate, so they cannot be entered under CAFTA-DR and pay the duty. Guatemala's own list (note 52(j)(6)(iii), 9903.06.06) also exempts 245 of the 252 subheadings when CAFTA-DR is claimed. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Guatemalan T-shirts and knit tops under CAFTA-DR pay nothing; without the claim the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 tariff (2026, 60 economies); CAFTA-DR apparel exempt
inEffect.exemption: CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods (general note 29(d)(v)) of El Salvador entered free of duty under CAFTA-DR — SPI P, or a subchapter XXII Chapter 98 provision such as short-supply heading 9822.05.01 — pay no Section 301 duty (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). That covers 821 of the 838 lines. The other 17 lines whose General rate is already Free — suits of artificial fibres and wool-blend synthetic suits (6103.10.40, .50, 6104.13.10, 6104.19.15), women's suit-type jackets of other textiles (6104.39.20), artificial-fibre babies' T-shirts (6111.90.30), surgical compression hosiery (6115.10.05), and ice- and field-hockey gloves and silk gloves (6116.10.05, .92.05, .93.05, .99.20, .99.75) — print no P rate, so they cannot be entered under CAFTA-DR and pay the duty. El Salvador's own list (note 52(j)(7)(iii), 9903.06.09) also exempts 245 of the 252 subheadings when CAFTA-DR is claimed. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Salvadoran T-shirts, socks and underwear under CAFTA-DR pay nothing; without the claim the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 61 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or on a country exception list for Sri Lanka. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. Sri Lanka's IEEPA rate had been 20% (9903.02.57).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Sri Lankan synthetic panties pay 25.6%, cotton T-shirts 26.5%.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94), including goods entered under the USMCA tariff preference levels (9823.53.01–.02). Under USMCA (General Note 11) knit apparel generally qualifies only if the yarn and fabric are from the region and the garment is cut (or knit to shape) and sewn there. Mexico is not subject to the Canada Section 338 duty. The 25% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: USMCA-qualifying Mexican T-shirts and sweaters pay nothing; non-qualifying goods pay the base rate plus 10% — 26.5% on cotton T-shirts.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 61 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or on a country exception list for Egypt. Egypt has no free trade agreement with the United States. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. Egypt's IEEPA rate had been the 10% baseline.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Egyptian cotton T-shirts and sweatshirts pay 29%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 tariff (2026, 60 economies); CAFTA-DR apparel exempt
inEffect.exemption: CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods (general note 29(d)(v)) of the Dominican Republic entered free of duty under CAFTA-DR — SPI P, or a subchapter XXII Chapter 98 provision such as short-supply heading 9822.05.01 — pay no Section 301 duty (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). That covers 821 of the 838 lines. The other 17 lines whose General rate is already Free — suits of artificial fibres and wool-blend synthetic suits (6103.10.40, .50, 6104.13.10, 6104.19.15), women's suit-type jackets of other textiles (6104.39.20), artificial-fibre babies' T-shirts (6111.90.30), surgical compression hosiery (6115.10.05), and ice- and field-hockey gloves and silk gloves (6116.10.05, .92.05, .93.05, .99.20, .99.75) — print no P rate, so they cannot be entered under CAFTA-DR and pay the duty. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. The Section 122 surcharge also exempted CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods (9903.03.09).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Dominican apparel that qualifies under CAFTA-DR pays nothing; non-qualifying goods pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: EU goods pay 10% in total in place of the base rate (9903.05.39) when the base rate is under 10%; at or above 10% nothing is added (note 52(k)). Most Chapter 61 cotton and synthetic lines are above 10%, so Italian and Portuguese knitwear usually pays just its base rate; cashmere sweaters (4%), silk garments and other low-rated lines pay 10%. The EU exception list (note 52(j)(2)) names no Chapter 61 subheading. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: An Italian wool sweater pays 16%, a cashmere one 10%, a cotton T-shirt 16.5%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 tariff (non-USMCA goods) + Section 338 duty (6 subheadings, USMCA or not)
inEffect.exemption: Two measures. The 2026 Section 301 duty (+10%, 9903.05.29) does not apply to USMCA-qualifying goods (9903.05.93). The Section 338 duty (+50%, from August 22, 2026, 9903.03.14) applies to products of Canada in six Chapter 61 subheadings — 6104.43.20 (women's synthetic dresses), 6104.63.20 (women's synthetic trousers and shorts), 6109.10.00 (cotton T-shirts), 6110.20.20 (cotton sweaters and sweatshirts), 6110.30.30 (man-made-fibre sweaters and sweatshirts) and 6116.93.88 (synthetic gloves without fourchettes) — 55 statistical lines, and U.S. note 51(a) applies it even when USMCA or another special rate is claimed (Chapter 98 entries are outside it, except USMCA entries of subchapter XXIII, such as the tariff preference levels, and 9802 entries). The September 15, 2026 list revisions (Proclamations 11064, 11065) added or removed no Chapter 61 provision. No Chapter 61 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes. The 35% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA goods ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A USMCA-qualifying Canadian cotton T-shirt or sweatshirt pays 50%; a non-qualifying one 76.5%. All other USMCA knitwear from Canada pays nothing.

inEffect.exemption: Brazil's 25% (9903.05.01, from July 22, 2026) reaches every Chapter 61 line; the Brazil exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)) names none. The 2026 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.27). The 2025 IEEPA duties (10% reciprocal and 40%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian knitwear pays 37.5% on top of the base rate — 54% on cotton T-shirts.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (incl. Peru, the Philippines, Thailand, Türkiye, Costa Rica, Malaysia, Taiwan, South Korea)
inEffect.now: +10% or 10% (in place of base) or +12.5% or 12.5% (in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: Jordan's exception list (note 52(j), 9903.06.20) and, when CAFTA-DR is claimed, the Guatemala and El Salvador lists (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09) cover 245 of the 252 Chapter 61 subheadings — every one except graduated compression hosiery (6115.10); no other country list names a Chapter 61 code. Costa Rica's CAFTA-DR apparel is exempt under note 52(i). Countries outside the 60 economies — Haiti, Kenya, Madagascar, Lesotho, Ethiopia, Myanmar and others — pay only the base rate. Peru, Colombia and other FTA partners keep the FTA's Free base rate but pay the Section 301 duty (note 52(a)). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Peruvian cotton T-shirts under the Peru TPA pay 12.5%; Thai and Turkish knitwear the base rate plus 12.5%; Kenyan or Haitian garments the base rate, or nothing under AGOA or HOPE/HELP.

changes.title: No Chapter 61 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 838 Chapter 61 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: CBP proposes new entry rules for low-value and mail shipments
changes.detail: CBP proposed to change filing requirements for informal entries of goods valued at $2,500 or less, create an electronic informal entry type for mail and add bonding requirements. Comments are due December 7, 2026. It would change how small parcels of clothing are entered, not their duty rate.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 4A continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018–2019 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 61 this keeps +7.5% (9903.88.15) on 714 of the 838 lines; List 4B stays suspended.

changes.title: Canadian import bans do not reach Chapter 61
changes.detail: Proclamations 11061–11063 banned some Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy-scope products and motorcycles over 800 cc from September 29, 2026. No Chapter 61 line is on their annexes.

changes.title: Section 338 list revised; Chapter 61 entries unchanged
changes.detail: Proclamations 11064 and 11065 added and removed provisions on the Section 338 lists from September 15, 2026. None of them is in Chapter 61, so the six Chapter 61 subheadings stay on the 9903.03.14 list in U.S. note 51(b)(3).

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty of 50% on cotton T-shirts, sweaters and four other knit subheadings
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on Canadian goods listed in U.S. note 51(b)(3), which names 6104.43.20 (women's synthetic dresses), 6104.63.20 (women's synthetic trousers and shorts), 6109.10.00 (cotton T-shirts), 6110.20.20 (cotton sweaters and sweatshirts), 6110.30.30 (man-made-fibre sweaters and sweatshirts) and 6116.93.88 (synthetic gloves without fourchettes) — 55 Chapter 61 lines. It is charged even when USMCA is claimed, and on top of the 10% Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods. Planned for August 19, it took effect August 22 after a 3-day suspension (Proclamation 11056).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies — CAFTA-DR and Jordanian apparel exempt
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84): 12.5% for Vietnam, China, Egypt, the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Thailand, Türkiye, Peru and the Philippines; 10% for Cambodia, Bangladesh, Indonesia, India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador, Jordan, Mexico and Canada; 10% in total for the EU. No Chapter 61 line is on the general exemption list. CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods entered free of duty are exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95); Jordan's exception list (note 52(j), 9903.06.20) and, when CAFTA-DR is claimed, the Guatemala and El Salvador lists (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09) cover 245 of the 252 Chapter 61 subheadings — every one except graduated compression hosiery (6115.10). USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94), and so are goods entered under a Chapter 98 provision other than 9802 — for example AGOA (9819.11) or Haiti HOPE/HELP (9820.61) apparel. Other FTA claims remove the base rate but not this duty.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 61 line is on the Brazil exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) and the apparel tariff preference levels still remove the base rate and the Section 301 duty on Mexican and Canadian knitwear.

changes.title: CBP suspends de minimis indefinitely
changes.detail: Two interim final rules suspend the $800 de minimis exemption in CBP's regulations: 19 CFR 10.151(b) for every mode except mail, and 19 CFR 145.31(b) for mail, until CBP announces otherwise. A T-shirt or hoodie shipped direct to a U.S. consumer needs an entry and pays the full duty — base rate plus the extra duty for its origin.

changes.title: CBP forced-labor guidance: cotton and apparel are high-priority sectors
changes.detail: CBP's operational guidance for importers lists the supply-chain tracing documents it expects for the UFLPA high-priority sectors, which include cotton and cotton products and apparel. Garments made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by a listed entity — including garments of Xinjiang cotton sewn in another country — are presumed barred unless the importer rebuts the presumption.

changes.title: AGOA and Haiti HOPE/HELP extensions written into the HTS
changes.detail: Proclamation 11030 (signed May 19, 2026) amended general note 16, the AGOA apparel note in Chapter 98 subchapter XIX and the Haiti note in subchapter XX so that AGOA, its regional-apparel and third-country-fabric programs, and the Haiti HOPE/HELP duty-free treatment run through December 31, 2026.

changes.title: CBP opens CAPE for IEEPA duty refunds
changes.detail: CBP deployed the Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries (CAPE) function in ACE: importers of record and their brokers file a CAPE Declaration listing entries, and ACE removes the IEEPA Chapter 99 lines and refunds the IEEPA duties with interest. Section 301, List 4A and Section 338 duties are not refunded.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 61 subheading was on the product exemption lists. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08) and CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods entered duty-free (9903.03.09) were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: De minimis suspension continued after the IEEPA ruling
changes.detail: Executive Order 14388 kept duty-free de minimis treatment suspended for all countries.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. India's 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA and Haiti HOPE/HELP reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75) renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025, with its regional-apparel and third-country-fabric programs, and extended the Haiti HOPE/HELP duty-free treatment through December 31, 2026. For knit apparel these programs work through Chapter 98 (9819.11.xx for AGOA, 9820.61.xx for Haiti) rather than the SPI D column, which is printed on only six Chapter 61 lines. GSP remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Scheduled: Section 301 tariff on products of Nicaragua
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty (9903.89.01) on Nicaraguan goods that are not entered under CAFTA-DR: 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028, on every Chapter 61 line. CAFTA-DR-originating apparel — most of Nicaragua's $1.7B of knitwear shipments — is not covered.

changes.title: China List 4A exclusion for babies' sleep sacks extended
changes.detail: USTR extended 178 China Section 301 product exclusions through November 9, 2026, including one in Chapter 61: babies' knit cotton sleep sacks with a neck opening and two-way zipper (6111.20.60.70). It removes the 7.5% List 4A duty (9903.88.69) but not the 12.5% 2026 duty.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It applied to every Chapter 61 line on top of List 4A until it ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: De minimis exemption suspended for all countries
changes.detail: Executive Order 14324 ended duty-free entry for shipments valued at $800 or less (19 U.S.C. 1321) from every country, effective for goods entered from August 29, 2025. Direct-to-consumer clothing parcels have paid duty since then.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84), on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025: 50% in all on Indian apparel, on top of the base rate. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set country rates for goods entered from August 7, 2025 — for the main knitwear suppliers Vietnam, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka +20%, Cambodia, Indonesia, Pakistan, Thailand and the Philippines +19%, Nicaragua +18%, Jordan, Lesotho and Madagascar +15%, India +25%, and 15% in total for EU goods; Central American Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador and the Dominican Republic stayed at the 10% baseline (Costa Rica 15%). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 added 40% on goods of Brazil, on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Law ends the de minimis exemption from July 1, 2027
changes.detail: Section 70531 of P.L. 119-21 terminates the de minimis exemption of 19 U.S.C. 1321(a)(2)(C) effective July 1, 2027, as CBP's 2026 rules note.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025. A Chinese cotton T-shirt then paid 16.5% + 7.5% (List 4A) + 20% + 10% = 54% until November 9, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% from April 10, 2025, on top of List 4A and the 20% fentanyl duty, and paused the higher country rates announced April 2 for others (Vietnam 46%, Cambodia 49%, Bangladesh 37%), which never took effect.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025, and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 61 product was exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of List 4A.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: UFLPA presumption takes effect
changes.detail: The Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act's rebuttable presumption applies from June 21, 2022: goods mined, produced or manufactured wholly or in part in Xinjiang, or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List, are presumed made with forced labor and barred. It succeeded CBP's December 2020 withhold release order on cotton products of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps and the January 2021 region-wide order on Xinjiang cotton.

changes.title: China List 4A duty cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: Under the Phase One agreement USTR cut the List 4A duty (9903.88.15) from 15% to 7.5%. The rate on the 714 Chapter 61 lines has been 7.5% ever since.

changes.title: China List 4B suspended before it took effect
changes.detail: USTR suspended indefinitely the 15% List 4B duty (9903.88.16) that was to start December 15, 2019. List 4B held 43 Chapter 61 subheadings — among them wholly cashmere sweaters, silk garments and hockey gloves — so those Chinese garments never paid a China list duty.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 4A reaches apparel
changes.detail: The fourth China Section 301 list put +15% on 209 Chapter 61 subheadings — most cotton and man-made-fibre T-shirts, sweaters, trousers, underwear, socks and babies' wear. No Chapter 61 line was on Lists 1–3.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of knitted and crocheted apparel were **$46.64B in 2025**, 1.6% less than the $47.37B of 2024 and well below the $60.78B peak of 2022. **Vietnam** overtook China as the largest supplier at **$9.84B** (21%, up 16%), while **China** fell 36% to **$6.81B** (15%) — in 2025 Chinese garments carried List 4A, the IEEPA fentanyl duty and, from April, the reciprocal tariff. **Cambodia** ($3.67B, up 31%), **Bangladesh** ($2.97B), **Indonesia** ($2.59B) and **India** ($2.50B) followed. The CAFTA-DR countries — Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic and Costa Rica — together shipped **$6.55B**, and **Jordan** $1.50B, and both can enter Free, with no Section 301 duty, when the garments meet the agreements' rules of origin.

By product, heading 6110 — sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, hoodies and cardigans — was **$13.28B**, more than a quarter of the chapter; cotton ones (6110.20) alone were $7.35B and man-made-fibre ones (6110.30) $4.77B. **T-shirts and tank tops** (6109) were $6.73B, of which cotton $4.86B; women's suits, dresses, skirts, trousers and leggings (6104) $5.67B; women's underwear and sleepwear (6108) $3.03B; men's trousers and ensembles (6103) $2.54B; and socks and hosiery (6115) $2.36B.

The IEEPA duties that pushed sourcing away from China in 2025 ended on February 24, 2026. Since July 24, 2026 the main extra duty is a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% on 60 economies that exempts CAFTA-DR and Jordanian apparel, and China keeps List 4A. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

seo.shortDescription: The total 2026 U.S. tariff on T-shirts, sweaters, hoodies, leggings, underwear and socks by country: Vietnam 29% on cotton tees, China 36.5%, Cambodia and Bangladesh 26.5%, CAFTA-DR and Jordan Free, USMCA Free (Canada 50% on six subheadings), with the 32% man-made-fibre lines priced too.

industryAreas.intro:
Knit apparel base rates are among the highest in the schedule — 16.5% on a cotton T-shirt, 32% on a polyester sweatshirt — and the extra duty **depends on where the garment was made**. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026): **Vietnam, Egypt and the Dominican Republic +12.5%**, **Cambodia, Bangladesh, Indonesia, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka +10%**, EU knitwear 10% in total. **China pays +20%** on most lines (12.5% plus List 4A). **CAFTA-DR apparel** from Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and the Dominican Republic, priced here with the CAFTA-DR claim, and **Jordanian** apparel are Free with no extra duty. **USMCA goods from Mexico pay nothing**, and Canada pays 50% under Section 338 on six subheadings even with USMCA. Haiti and Kenya are outside the 60 economies and pay only the base rate — or nothing under the Haiti and AGOA Chapter 98 programs, which the grid does not apply.

The 17 lines whose General rate is already Free — suits of artificial fibres and wool-blend synthetic suits (6103.10.40, .50, 6104.13.10, 6104.19.15), women's suit-type jackets of other textiles (6104.39.20), artificial-fibre babies' T-shirts (6111.90.30), surgical compression hosiery (6115.10.05), and ice- and field-hockey gloves and silk gloves (6116.10.05, .92.05, .93.05, .99.20, .99.75) — carry no P rate and pay 12.5% (9903.05.58). Goods that do not meet the CAFTA-DR rules of origin pay the base rate plus 12.5%. Non-CAFTA-DR goods will also pay the Nicaragua Section 301 duty (9903.89.01) of 10% from January 1, 2027.

The 17 lines whose General rate is already Free — suits of artificial fibres and wool-blend synthetic suits (6103.10.40, .50, 6104.13.10, 6104.19.15), women's suit-type jackets of other textiles (6104.39.20), artificial-fibre babies' T-shirts (6111.90.30), surgical compression hosiery (6115.10.05), and ice- and field-hockey gloves and silk gloves (6116.10.05, .92.05, .93.05, .99.20, .99.75) — carry no P rate and pay 10% (9903.05.40). Goods that do not meet the CAFTA-DR rules of origin pay the base rate plus 10%.

rule.label: With a CAFTA-DR claim (SPI P), as shown: no base rate and no Section 301 duty on 821 of the 838 lines — CAFTA-DR apparel entered free of duty is exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). The 17 lines whose General rate is already Free — suits of artificial fibres and wool-blend synthetic suits (6103.10.40, .50, 6104.13.10, 6104.19.15), women's suit-type jackets of other textiles (6104.39.20), artificial-fibre babies' T-shirts (6111.90.30), surgical compression hosiery (6115.10.05), and ice- and field-hockey gloves and silk gloves (6116.10.05, .92.05, .93.05, .99.20, .99.75) — carry no P rate and pay 12.5% (9903.05.34). Goods that do not meet the CAFTA-DR rules of origin pay the base rate plus 12.5%.

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-13, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.

Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; P for Honduras; P for Nicaragua; JO for Jordan; P for Guatemala; P for El Salvador; P for Dominican Republic; D for Kenya. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Conditional relief is not applied (it needs the importer's confirmation): 9903.88.69 (Section 301).
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Knit ensembles (6103.22–6103.29, 6104.22–6104.29) have the base rate "the rate applicable to each garment in the ensemble if separately entered". The cells show that text plus the extra duty, because the base duty depends on the garments in the set. The tariff calculator prices it: enter each garment's 10-digit line and value (the values add up to the shipment value, and per-kilogram rates ask for the weight); each garment pays its own rate on its own value, and the extra duties are charged on the whole value. Under an FTA claim the ensemble line itself is Free.

CAFTA-DR countries are priced with the CAFTA-DR claim (SPI P): the base rate is Free and note 52(i) removes the Section 301 duty. Lines whose General rate is already Free print no P, so they cannot be entered under CAFTA-DR and keep the duty.

Chapter 98 programs are not in the grid: AGOA apparel (9819.11.xx), Haiti HOPE/HELP (9820.61.xx) and CBTPA (9820.11.xx), the USMCA tariff preference levels (9823.52–9823.53) and U.S.-component assembly (9802.00.80). Goods properly entered under a Chapter 98 provision other than 9802 also escape the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(a)).

The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied. The Nicaragua Section 301 duty (9903.89.01) starts January 1, 2027 and is not applied.
EU rates of "10% in total" replace the base rate when it is lower (U.S. note 52(k)); where the base rate is higher, only the base rate applies.

Not in the grid: the UFLPA presumption against garments containing Xinjiang cotton, CBP textile entry rules, and FTC and CPSC labeling and flammability rules — see Import documents. No antidumping or countervailing duty order and no Section 232 action covers a Chapter 61 product.
industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 16, 19, 20, 30, 31, 33, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. Note 52(b) (9903.05.86) names no Chapter 61 code, and the carve-outs in 52(c)–(f) do not reach apparel. Note 52(i) (9903.05.95) exempts CAFTA-DR textile and apparel goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua entered free of duty under CAFTA-DR. Of the note 52(j) country lists, only Jordan's (9903.06.20) and — for CAFTA-DR claims — Guatemala's (9903.06.06) and El Salvador's (9903.06.09) name Chapter 61 codes: 245 of the 252 subheadings, all but 6115.10; the UK, EU, Swiss, Malaysian, Cambodian, Argentine, Bangladeshi, Taiwanese, Indonesian and Ecuadorian lists name none. Note 50(a)(ii) names no Chapter 61 code for Brazil. Note 51(b)(3) puts 6104.43.20, 6104.63.20, 6109.10.00, 6110.20.20, 6110.30.30 and 6116.93.88 on the Canada Section 338 list (9903.03.14). Note 20(s) puts 209 Chapter 61 subheadings on List 4A; the other 43 are on List 4B (note 20(u)), which is suspended; no Chapter 61 line is on Lists 1–3, and note 20(vvv)(iv) excludes one product (babies' sleep sacks, 6111.20.60.70) through November 9, 2026. Note 31 (2024 increases) and note 30 (Russia, 9903.90.08) list no Chapter 61 line. No Section 232 heading (notes 16, 19, 33, 36–39) reaches a Chapter 61 product; the Section 232 certified-parts elections are opt-in and left out. A Federal Register search of Commerce (ITA) notices found no antidumping or countervailing duty order on a Chapter 61 product.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Knitted Apparel (HTS Ch. 61): Origin Rules, UFLPA, Labeling, Flammability & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Clothing: Apparel Origin Rules, UFLPA, FTC Labels, CPSC Flammability & Duty Savings (HTS 61) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The CBP, FTC and CPSC rules for knitted apparel — country of origin where the garment is assembled (19 CFR 102.21), manufacturer ID, UFLPA cotton tracing, fibre, origin and care labels (16 CFR 303, 423), children's sleepwear and drawstring rules — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, CAFTA-DR, Jordan, AGOA, Haiti HOPE/HELP, first sale, U.S. components, drawback and FTZs.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For most knitted garments **the country of origin is the country where the garment was wholly assembled** — sewn or linked from its cut or knit-to-shape pieces — and for knit-to-shape garments the country where the pieces were knit (19 CFR 102.21). That is different from home textiles and fabric, whose origin follows the fabric. Every entry must name the manufacturer by manufacturer identification code, cotton garments face the UFLPA presumption against Xinjiang cotton, and every garment sold at retail needs a fibre-content, origin and care label (16 CFR parts 303 and 423); children's sleepwear and children's outerwear with drawstrings have CPSC rules of their own.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: **USMCA** and its tariff preference levels for Mexico and Canada, **CAFTA-DR** for Central American and Dominican apparel (Free, and exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty), **Jordan's** FTA and exception list, the **AGOA** and **Haiti HOPE/HELP** Chapter 98 programs (through December 31, 2026), **assembly from U.S.-cut components** (9802.00.80), **first-sale valuation**, **drawback** and **foreign-trade zones**. Each depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Know where the garment is assembled — that is usually the country of origin
levers.saves: The difference between country rates: nothing for CAFTA-DR, Jordan or USMCA goods, +10% for Cambodia or Bangladesh, +12.5% for Vietnam, +20% for China
levers.appliesTo: All of Chapter 61: garments of two or more pieces take the origin of the country where they are wholly assembled; knit-to-shape garments the country where the pieces are knit; one-piece garments the country where the fabric is formed
levers.document: Production records for each step (cutting, knitting, sewing or linking) and the MID of the company that did the origin-conferring step, on the entry.
levers.caveat: Assembly must happen wholly in one country; partial sewing or finishing does not move origin. CBP denies entry to goods of companies named for illegal transshipment (19 CFR 102.24), and goods with Xinjiang cotton are barred wherever they are sewn.

levers.title: Claim USMCA — or a USMCA tariff preference level — on knitwear made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 32%) and the 10% Section 301 duty on Mexican and Canadian goods
levers.appliesTo: Originating goods under General Note 11 — for knit apparel generally yarn and fabric from the region, cut (or knit to shape) and sewn there — and, within annual limits, non-originating apparel cut and sewn in Mexico (45 million SME of cotton or man-made-fibre apparel, 9823.53.01) or Canada (40 million SME, 9823.52.01) from imported fabric
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, with SPI "S" (originating) or "S+" (tariff preference level) on the entry line.
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on 6104.43.20 (women's synthetic dresses), 6104.63.20 (women's synthetic trousers and shorts), 6109.10.00 (cotton T-shirts), 6110.20.20 (cotton sweaters and sweatshirts), 6110.30.30 (man-made-fibre sweaters and sweatshirts) and 6116.93.88 (synthetic gloves without fourchettes). The Mexican TPL excludes T-shirts (6109.10, 6109.90.10) and men's briefs (6107.11, 6107.12) made chiefly of circular knit fabric of yarn number 100 metric or less. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

provisions.text: Cotton or man-made-fibre apparel of Mexico, up to 45,000,000 SME a year
Cotton or man-made-fibre apparel of Canada, up to 40,000,000 SME a year

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 98 subch. XXIII, U.S. note 11

levers.title: Claim CAFTA-DR — it removes the base rate and the 2026 Section 301 duty
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 32%) and the 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty on Central American and Dominican apparel
levers.appliesTo: Apparel of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua that originates under General Note 29 (generally yarn-forward: yarn and fabric from the region or the U.S., cut and sewn in the region), or that uses short-supply fabrics (9822.05.01), entered free of duty under CAFTA-DR
levers.document: Proof of origin under CAFTA-DR and SPI "P" on the entry line; the Section 301 relief is reported with 9903.05.95, or 9903.06.06 / 9903.06.09 for Guatemala and El Salvador.
levers.caveat: The 17 Chapter 61 lines that are Free at the General rate print no P and keep the Section 301 duty. Non-CAFTA-DR goods of Nicaragua will pay 10% more from January 1, 2027 (9903.89.01).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(i), (j)

levers.title: Source from Jordan — FTA Free and on the Section 301 exception list
levers.saves: The base rate and the 10% Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: Garments of Jordan meeting the US–Jordan FTA rule of origin (SPI JO); the Section 301 exception list (9903.06.20) covers every Chapter 61 subheading except graduated compression hosiery (6115.10)
levers.document: Proof that the goods meet the US–Jordan FTA origin rules and SPI "JO" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: Compression hosiery from Jordan still pays the 10% Section 301 duty.

levers.title: Use the AGOA or Haiti apparel provisions of Chapter 98
levers.saves: The full base rate — AGOA and Haiti are outside the 60 Section 301 economies, and Chapter 98 entries other than 9802 are outside the 2026 Section 301 duty anyway
levers.appliesTo: Apparel of AGOA beneficiary countries that meet the apparel requirements (Kenya, Lesotho, Madagascar and others in Chapter 98 subchapter XIX note 1), including lesser developed beneficiaries using third-country fabric (9819.11.12); apparel wholly assembled or knit-to-shape in Haiti and imported directly from Haiti or the Dominican Republic (9820.61.25–9820.61.45), or under CBTPA (9820.11.xx)
levers.document: The AGOA textile certificate of origin and visa (19 CFR 10.213, 10.214) or the Haiti/CBTPA documentation, with the Chapter 98 heading on the entry.
levers.caveat: AGOA and HOPE/HELP run through December 31, 2026 under P.L. 119-75 and Proclamation 11030; the AGOA third-country fabric and Haiti HOPE programs have annual quantity limits. CBTPA runs through September 30, 2030. Some HELP coverage excludes men's basic cotton T-shirts and sweatshirts (note 6(j)(ii)).

provisions.text: AGOA apparel of lesser developed beneficiary countries, regardless of fabric origin (annual cap)
AGOA apparel of regional fabric (annual cap)
Chapter 61 apparel wholly assembled or knit-to-shape in Haiti, any fabric (HELP, annual cap)
Haiti apparel meeting the value-content rule (HOPE)

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 98, subchapters XIX and XX

levers.title: Claim another free trade agreement where the base rate is the cost
levers.saves: The base rate — 16.5% on a cotton T-shirt, 32% on a polyester sweatshirt
levers.appliesTo: Apparel of Peru, Colombia, Panama, Korea, Israel, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman, Chile, Australia and Singapore under each agreement's (mostly yarn-forward) rule of origin
levers.document: The origin proof each program requires and the SPI on the entry line (PE, CO, PA, KR, IL, MA, BH, OM, CL, AU, SG).
levers.caveat: These claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)): Peruvian FTA T-shirts still pay 12.5%. GSP (A, A*) has been expired since December 31, 2020 and the Nepal program (NP) since December 31, 2025.

levers.title: Assemble abroad from U.S.-formed and cut components (9802.00.80)
levers.saves: Duty on the value of the U.S. components; base rate and Section 301 duty are charged only on the value added abroad
levers.appliesTo: Garments assembled abroad from fabric components cut to shape in the United States and exported ready for assembly (statistical notes 4 and 5 cover the related Special Access and Outward Processing reporting)
levers.document: The foreign assembler's declaration and the importer's endorsement (19 CFR 10.24), with the value of the U.S. components.
levers.caveat: Components must not be advanced in value abroad except by assembly and incidental operations; the 2026 Section 301 and Section 338 duties apply to the value of the foreign assembly.

levers.title: Enter knit ensembles as ensembles — each garment pays its own rate
levers.saves: Nothing by itself, but pricing the set correctly avoids paying the highest garment rate on the whole set
levers.appliesTo: Sets of note 3(b) — one upper and one or two lower garments of identical fabric, put up for retail sale (6103.22–6103.29, 6104.22–6104.29)
levers.document: The invoice must break the set into garments, each with its 10-digit line and value; report each under the most appropriate 10-digit number of the ensemble subheading (statistical note 1).
levers.caveat: The duty is the sum of each garment's rate on its value plus the extra duties on the whole value. Sets that are not ensembles (for example a T-shirt with shorts, since 6109 articles are excluded) are classified garment by garment anyway.

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 61, notes 3(b) and statistical note 1

levers.title: Check fibre content and garment type line by line
levers.saves: Up to 16 points: a man-made-fibre T-shirt or sweater is 32% and its cotton twin 16.5%; a wholly cashmere sweater 4% against 16% for other wool
levers.appliesTo: Every line — the fibre that predominates by weight decides the subheading, and note 4, note 5 and the sweater stitch-count note decide shirt vs. T-shirt vs. sweater
levers.document: A binding ruling request to CBP (19 CFR part 177) with fibre content by weight, stitch count and construction; invoices must state fibre content (19 CFR 141.89).
levers.caveat: Classification follows the goods as imported. A blend changes subheading only if it changes the fibre that predominates by weight, and labels must still state the true fibre content.

levers.title: Use the China List 4A exclusion for babies' sleep sacks
levers.saves: The 7.5% List 4A duty (the 12.5% 2026 duty still applies)
levers.appliesTo: Babies' knit cotton sleep sacks with a neck opening and two-way zipper, as the exclusion describes them (6111.20.60.70), entered by November 9, 2026
levers.document: Heading 9903.88.69 reported with the statistical number, and records showing the goods match the exclusion's description.
levers.caveat: The exclusion ends after November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends it again.

levers.title: Value at the first sale for export when you buy through a middleman
levers.saves: Every ad valorem duty — base rate and Section 301 — is charged on a lower value when the factory's price to a trading company or agent is lower than the price you pay
levers.appliesTo: All lines bought through a trading company, agent-buyer or brand owner rather than straight from the factory
levers.document: Proof that the first sale was a bona fide sale for export to the United States at arm's length: the factory invoice, contracts and payment records.
levers.caveat: Only a sale clearly destined for the U.S. qualifies, and the importer must be able to show the earlier price at entry.

levers.title: Claim drawback when the garments are exported or destroyed
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on apparel re-exported unused
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded.

levers.title: Hold, label or kit apparel in a foreign-trade zone
levers.saves: No duty on goods re-exported from the zone, and duty deferred until goods enter the U.S. market
levers.appliesTo: Any line — useful for stock distributed to Canada, Mexico and the U.S. from one warehouse
levers.document: Zone admission (CBP Form 214) and the zone operator's inventory records.
levers.caveat: Goods entered for U.S. consumption from a zone pay the duties in force on the entry date.

rules.title: Country of origin of knit apparel (6101–6117): where the garment is wholly assembled if it has two or more components; where the knit-to-shape components are knit if knit to shape; where the fabric is formed if it is a single piece; scarves, shawls and veils of 6117.10 (other than cotton or wool) take the country where the fabric was dyed and printed with two finishing operations
Manufacturer identification code (MID) of the company that performed the origin-conferring operation on every entry and entry summary — this replaced the textile declaration, eliminated in 2011
Entry is denied for textiles and apparel from a company named in the Federal Register for illegal transshipment or for being unable to verify production
Invoice details for apparel: fibre content by weight, whether knit or woven, the garment type and gender, the manufacturer and the country of origin

UFLPA: garments made wholly or in part in Xinjiang — including garments of Xinjiang cotton sewn elsewhere — or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are presumed made with forced labor and excluded unless the importer rebuts it; cotton and apparel are high-priority sectors, so cotton garments need cotton tracing documents

Textile Act labels on all wearing apparel: generic fibre names and percentages, the RN or company name, and the country where processed or made ("Made in Vietnam"); permanently knotted neckties and garters are excluded
Wool Products Labeling Act: wool, cashmere and other wool-containing sweaters, coats, socks and scarves must show wool fibre content and origin
Care Labeling Rule: a permanent care label with washing or drycleaning instructions on textile wearing apparel sold to consumers, attached by the manufacturer or importer
Flammability of clothing textiles: all clothing textiles must meet the Class 1 or Class 2 test; hats, gloves up to 14 inches and footwear (other than hosiery) are excepted
Children's sleepwear sizes 0–6X and 7–14 (nightgowns, pajamas, robes) must pass the stricter sleepwear flammability standards, except infant garments of 9 months or smaller and tight-fitting garments

Children's apparel: children's upper outerwear in sizes 2T–16 with hood, neck, waist or bottom drawstrings that do not meet ASTM F1816 is a substantial product hazard, and children's products need a Children's Product Certificate based on third-party testing
Country-of-origin marking: each garment must be marked with its English name of origin, in addition to the FTC label

groups.label: Men's and boys' knit coats, anoraks, ski jackets and windbreakers
groups.note: Coats take the origin of the country where they are wholly assembled. Children's jackets and hoodies with drawstrings must meet ASTM F1816. Wool coats need Wool Act labels.

groups.label: Women's and girls' knit coats, anoraks, ski jackets and windbreakers
groups.note: Same rules as 6101; right-over-left closure makes a coat women's (note 9).

groups.label: Men's and boys' knit suits, ensembles, blazers, trousers and shorts
groups.note: Ensembles (6103.22–.29) are priced garment by garment; suits must be of identical fabric (note 3). Origin is where the garments are wholly assembled.

groups.label: Women's and girls' knit suits, ensembles, dresses, skirts, trousers, leggings and shorts
groups.note: Ensembles (6104.22–.29) are priced garment by garment. Synthetic trousers and leggings (6104.63.20) and synthetic dresses (6104.43.20) from Canada owe the 50% Section 338 duty.

groups.label: Men's and boys' knit shirts (polo shirts)
groups.note: Shirts with a ribbed waistband or under 10 stitches per cm go elsewhere (note 4), usually 6110. Cotton 19.7%, man-made fibres 32%.

groups.label: Women's and girls' knit blouses and shirts
groups.note: Same construction rules as 6105 (note 4); sleeveless blouses are allowed in 6106.

groups.label: Men's and boys' underwear, pajamas and bathrobes, knit
groups.note: Children's pajamas and robes are children's sleepwear under 16 CFR 1615/1616. Cotton underwear needs UFLPA cotton tracing.

groups.label: Women's and girls' slips, panties, nightdresses, pajamas and robes, knit
groups.note: Children's nightgowns and pajamas must meet the sleepwear flammability standards unless tight-fitting. Bras are 6212, not here.

groups.label: T-shirts, singlets and tank tops, knit
groups.note: Garments with a drawstring or ribbed waistband at the bottom are not T-shirts (note 5). Cotton T-shirts (6109.10.00) from Canada owe 50% under Section 338 even with USMCA; the USMCA TPL for Mexico excludes some basic cotton T-shirts.

groups.label: Sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, hoodies, cardigans and vests, knit
groups.note: Sweaters (9 or fewer stitches per 2 cm), sweatshirts and hoodies. Knit-to-shape sweaters take the origin of the country where the panels were knit. 6110.20.20 and 6110.30.30 from Canada owe the Section 338 duty.

groups.label: Babies' garments and clothing accessories, knit
groups.note: Babies' wear is for a body height up to 86 cm and takes priority over other headings (note 6). Infant sleepwear of 9 months or smaller is exempt from the sleepwear standard if it meets the size and length limits.

groups.label: Track suits, ski suits and swimwear, knit
groups.note: Swimwear and track suits; a ski suit must be identifiable as for skiing (note 7). Track suits are reported garment by garment (statistical note 1).

groups.label: Garments of coated, rubberized or laminated knit fabric
groups.note: Garments of coated or laminated knit fabric take this heading before others except 6111 (note 8).

groups.label: Other knit garments (tops, bodysuits, jumpsuits, scrubs)
groups.note: Other knit garments; man-made-fibre tops and bodysuits carry 28.2%–32%.

groups.label: Socks, tights, pantyhose and other hosiery, knit
groups.note: Socks and hosiery. Graduated compression hosiery (6115.10) is the only Chapter 61 group outside the Jordan, Guatemala and El Salvador exception lists.

groups.label: Gloves, mittens and mitts, knit
groups.note: Knit gloves; leather gloves are 4203 and rubber or nitrile gloves 4015. Gloves up to 14 inches are outside the clothing flammability standard. 6116.93.88 from Canada owes the Section 338 duty.

groups.label: Scarves, shawls, ties, headbands and other knit accessories; parts
groups.note: Scarves, ties, headbands and knit parts of garments. Scarves and shawls of 6117.10 other than cotton or wool take the origin of the country that dyed and printed the fabric with two finishing steps (19 CFR 102.21(e)(2)).

finalConclusion.h1: HTS Chapter 61 FAQ: HS Codes & Import Tariffs for T-Shirts, Hoodies, Sweaters, Socks & Knit Clothing

seo.title: T-Shirt, Hoodie, Sweater & Socks HS Code and Clothing Tariff FAQ 2026 (HTS Chapter 61) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about importing knitted clothing: the HS code for T-shirts, hoodies, sweaters, socks, leggings, underwear, pajamas, swimwear, baby clothes and gloves, and the 2026 tariffs on clothing from China, Vietnam, India, Bangladesh and Mexico.
keywords: tariff on clothing from china to usa
tariff on clothes from india to usa

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing knitted and crocheted clothing into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 61 base rates run from Free to 32% and are unchanged since January 2025: cotton T-shirts, sweatshirts and hoodies 16.5%, the same of man-made fibres 32%, synthetic leggings 28.2%, cotton socks 13.5%.

Since July 24, 2026 Vietnam pays 12.5% Section 301 on top of the base rate; Cambodia, Bangladesh, Indonesia, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka 10%. China pays 20% on 714 of 838 lines (12.5% plus List 4A).

CAFTA-DR apparel entered duty-free (Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic, Costa Rica) and Jordanian apparel pay no base rate and no Section 301 duty; USMCA apparel from Mexico pays nothing.

Canada owes 50% under Section 338 on cotton T-shirts, cotton and man-made-fibre sweaters and sweatshirts, women's synthetic dresses and trousers and synthetic gloves, even with USMCA. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026.

Knit ensembles pay each garment's own rate. Origin is where the garment is assembled (19 CFR 102.21); cotton garments face the UFLPA presumption, and de minimis stays suspended for parcels shipped direct to consumers.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 61 cover?
faqs.answer: Clothing and clothing accessories that are knitted or crocheted: coats (6101–6102), suits, ensembles, trousers, dresses and skirts (6103–6104), knit shirts and blouses (6105–6106), underwear and sleepwear (6107–6108), T-shirts (6109), sweaters, sweatshirts and hoodies (6110), babies' wear (6111), track suits and swimwear (6112), other garments (6113–6114), socks (6115), gloves (6116) and scarves and accessories (6117). Woven clothing is Chapter 62; bras are 6212.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for T-shirts?
faqs.answer: Knit T-shirts, singlets and tank tops are heading 6109: cotton 6109.10.00 (16.5%) and man-made fibres 6109.90.10 (32%). In the U.S. 10-digit codes, men's cotton T-shirts are 6109.10.00.12 and women's 6109.10.00.40. Babies' T-shirts are 6111; a top with a drawstring or ribbed waistband at the bottom is not a T-shirt.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for hoodies and sweatshirts?
faqs.answer: Knit hoodies and sweatshirts are heading 6110: cotton 6110.20.20 (16.5%, men's 6110.20.20.41) and man-made fibres 6110.30.30 (32%, men's 6110.30.30.41). From Vietnam a cotton hoodie pays 29% in all, from China 36.5%, a polyester one from China 52%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for sweaters, cardigans and pullovers?
faqs.answer: Heading 6110: wool 6110.11 (16%), wholly cashmere 6110.12.10 (4%), cotton 6110.20.20 (16.5%), man-made fibres 6110.30.30 (32%). A sweater has 9 or fewer stitches per 2 cm on its outer surface (statistical note 3). Chinese cashmere sweaters were on the suspended List 4B, so they pay 4% + 12.5%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for socks?
faqs.answer: Heading 6115: cotton socks 6115.95.90 (13.5%, 10% with lace), synthetic socks 6115.96.90 (14.6%, 18.8% with lace), wool 6115.94 (11.3%), compression socks 6115.10. Babies' socks are 6111. From Pakistan cotton socks pay 23.5% in all; from China 33.5%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for leggings and knit pants?
faqs.answer: Women's knit trousers and leggings are 6104.62.20 if cotton (14.9%) and 6104.63.20 if synthetic (28.2%); men's are 6103.42.10 (cotton, 16.1%) and 6103.43.15 (synthetic, 28.2%). Tights and pantyhose are hosiery of 6115. Synthetic leggings pay 40.7% in all from Vietnam and 48.2% from China.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for baby clothes?
faqs.answer: Heading 6111 covers knit garments and accessories for babies up to 86 cm tall, and it takes priority over other headings. Cotton sets, rompers and other babies' wear are 6111.20.60 (8.1%), cotton T-shirts and trousers 14.9%, synthetic T-shirts and shirts 32%. Children's sleepwear must also meet CPSC flammability rules.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for underwear, boxers and panties?
faqs.answer: Men's knit underpants and briefs are 6107.11 (cotton, 7.4%) and 6107.12 (man-made fibres, 14.9%); women's briefs and panties 6108.21 (cotton, 7.6%) and 6108.22 (man-made fibres, 15.6%). Bras are 6212, outside this chapter.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for pajamas and sleepwear?
faqs.answer: Knit pajamas and nightshirts for men and boys are 6107.21–6107.29 (cotton 8.9%, man-made fibres 16%); nightdresses and pajamas for women and girls 6108.31–6108.39 (cotton 8.5%, man-made fibres 16%). Children's pajamas sizes 0–14 must pass the CPSC children's sleepwear standards unless tight-fitting.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for swimwear?
faqs.answer: Knit swimwear is heading 6112: men's synthetic 6112.31 (25.9%), women's and girls' synthetic swimsuits and bikinis 6112.41 (24.9%), other fibres 13.2%. Woven swim trunks are 6211.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for knit gloves and mittens?
faqs.answer: Knit gloves, mittens and mitts are heading 6116: synthetic 6116.93 (18.6%), cotton 6116.92, coated work gloves 6116.10 (7%–23.5%). Leather gloves are 4203 and rubber or nitrile gloves 4015. Canadian synthetic gloves (6116.93.88) owe the 50% Section 338 duty.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on clothing from China in 2026?
searchedAs: tariff on clothing from china to usa
current tariff on clothing from china
us tariff on clothing from china
faqs.answer: Knit clothing from China pays its base rate plus 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action (9903.05.31) and, on 714 of the 838 Chapter 61 lines, 7.5% under List 4A: 36.5% on a cotton T-shirt, 52% on a polyester hoodie, 33.5% on cotton socks. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and de minimis is suspended for parcels.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on clothes from India to the USA?
searchedAs: tariff on clothes from india to usa
tariffs on clothes from india to us
tariff on garments from india to usa
us tariff on garments from india
faqs.answer: Indian knit garments pay the base rate plus 10% Section 301 (9903.05.44), with no exception list: 26.5% on cotton T-shirts, 18.5% on cotton nightdresses. India's 50% IEEPA rate of late 2025 ended in February 2026, and GSP has been expired since 2020.

faqs.question: What are the apparel tariffs by country — Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Mexico?
faqs.answer: Add the Section 301 rate to the base rate: Vietnam +12.5%, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Pakistan and Sri Lanka +10%, EU 10% in total. A cotton T-shirt is 29% from Vietnam and 26.5% from Bangladesh or Cambodia. USMCA-qualifying Mexican apparel and CAFTA-DR or Jordanian apparel pay nothing.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import knitted clothing from?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the U.S. imported $46.64B of knitted apparel: Vietnam $9.84B, China $6.81B (down 36%), Cambodia $3.67B, Bangladesh $2.97B, Indonesia $2.59B and India $2.50B; the CAFTA-DR countries together shipped $6.55B.
